harm_patterns.name: Manipulation
harm_patterns.definition: A person or accountable principal is steered toward an outcome through materially misleading, asymmetric or exploitative influence.
example_manifestations: agent recommendation optimized against the principal

harm_patterns.name: Coercion
harm_patterns.definition: A person faces material penalty, loss or threat unless they accept a system action, disclosure or decision.

harm_patterns.name: Loss of meaningful choice
harm_patterns.definition: Nominal consent or choice exists but practical alternatives, information or timing are insufficient for meaningful agency.

harm_patterns.name: Delegation beyond informed intent
harm_patterns.definition: A delegated actor performs or enables an action outside the principal’s reasonably understood mandate.

harm_patterns.name: Inability to withdraw or revoke
harm_patterns.definition: A person cannot effectively terminate consent, delegated authority, participation or continued processing.

harm_patterns.name: Wrongful exclusion
harm_patterns.definition: A legitimate person or organization is denied access, participation or recognition without a justified basis.

harm_patterns.name: Discriminatory burden
harm_patterns.definition: A rule or system imposes materially higher burdens on a protected, marginalized or structurally disadvantaged group.

harm_patterns.name: Accessibility failure
harm_patterns.definition: A legitimate participant cannot complete a required interaction because accessibility needs are not supported.

harm_patterns.name: Infrastructure dependency exclusion
harm_patterns.definition: Access depends on devices, networks, identity infrastructure or services unavailable to some legitimate participants.

harm_patterns.name: Unnecessary disclosure
harm_patterns.definition: Information beyond the minimum necessary is exposed to a party or system.

harm_patterns.name: Linkability and correlation
harm_patterns.definition: Separate interactions can be linked to construct a broader profile of a person, organization or agent.

harm_patterns.name: Inference beyond disclosed facts
harm_patterns.definition: Observed data or metadata enables sensitive conclusions not intentionally disclosed.

harm_patterns.name: Persistent surveillance
harm_patterns.definition: System operation enables durable observation or reconstruction of activities across time or contexts.

harm_patterns.name: Secondary use and context collapse
harm_patterns.definition: Information collected for one purpose or audience is reused in another materially different context.
example_manifestations: public metadata used for unrelated profiling

harm_patterns.name: Loss of economic opportunity
harm_patterns.definition: A system decision prevents or materially reduces access to employment, trade, finance or other economic participation.

harm_patterns.name: Fraudulent or misallocated liability
harm_patterns.definition: A person or organization bears financial or legal consequences for an action they did not authorize or control.

harm_patterns.name: Arbitrary decision
harm_patterns.definition: A consequential decision is taken without consistent rules, sufficient reasons or accountable authority.

harm_patterns.name: Unavailable appeal or remedy
harm_patterns.definition: An affected party lacks a practical path to contest, correct or obtain remedy for an adverse outcome.

harm_patterns.name: Unaccountable or captured authority
harm_patterns.definition: Decision power is exercised without effective oversight, contestability or independence.
example_manifestations: single operator controls policy and evidence

harm_patterns.name: Impersonation and false attribution
harm_patterns.definition: Actions or claims are attributed to the wrong person, organization or agent.

harm_patterns.name: Unauthorized consequential action
harm_patterns.definition: A system performs a consequential action without current, sufficient authority from the accountable principal.

harm_patterns.name: Denial or disruption of participation
harm_patterns.definition: Security or operational failure prevents legitimate use, continuity, recovery or participation.

harm_patterns.name: False provenance or trust inference
harm_patterns.definition: A party correctly observes an artefact or signature but infers legitimacy, endorsement, authority or quality that it does not establish.
example_manifestations: signed agent card treated as authorization

harm_patterns.name: Physical or safeguarding exposure
harm_patterns.definition: Digital information or system action materially increases risk of physical harm, stalking, abuse or safeguarding failure.

risk_patterns.description: Authentication, key possession or identity proof is treated as sufficient evidence that the actor is authorized for the requested action.

risk_patterns.description: A credential obtained for one agent/task is forwarded or treated as authority for another without explicit onward delegation.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Opaque execution accountability gap
risk_patterns.description: Opaque internal execution is combined with insufficient external action provenance to reconstruct accountability.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Dependency unavailability or stale fallback
risk_patterns.description: A required registry, status, issuer, policy or network dependency is unavailable and fallback behavior is unsafe or undefined.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Replay or duplicate side effect
risk_patterns.description: A valid request, proof or task can be replayed or retried in a way that repeats an externally consequential effect.

risk_patterns.name: Cascading invalidation
risk_patterns.description: Compromise, deregistration or withdrawal of a dependency invalidates many downstream artefacts without a safe continuity path.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Evidence insufficient for contestability
risk_patterns.description: The system cannot produce durable evidence necessary to explain, contest or remedy a consequential outcome.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Cross-spec authority mismatch
risk_patterns.description: Two specifications use compatible-looking identity or authorization concepts with materially different semantics.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Cross-spec lifecycle mismatch
risk_patterns.description: Validity, status, expiry, revocation or freshness is evaluated at different lifecycle points across dependent specifications.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Cross-system linkability
risk_patterns.description: Composition across protocols exposes identifiers or metadata that defeat privacy separation present in each component.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Policy or evidence boundary conflict
risk_patterns.description: Dependent systems disagree about which artefact establishes completion, authority, status or an auditable fact.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Infrastructure dependency capture
risk_patterns.description: A critical governance or verification dependency is controlled by an actor that can extract rents, surveil participants or change access conditions.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: This risk can create an unacceptable state at a clear decision or execution boundary, so a portable guardrail should block or stop that state.

risk_patterns.name: Failure cost externalization
risk_patterns.description: Operators or intermediaries capture benefits while harmed participants bear disproportionate remediation, exclusion or liability costs.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Failure costs are not always avoidable. A guardrail is required when affected people cannot reasonably choose, exit or seek remedy.
guardrail_requirement.condition: Applies to high-impact or involuntary use where materially affected parties lack meaningful choice, exit or remedy.

risk_patterns.name: Attribution lineage mistaken for authority
risk_patterns.description: Caller-supplied delegation or actor-lineage metadata is treated as proof that the represented grants actually existed or remain valid.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Attribution metadata can be syntactically valid while fabricated, so consequential action requires independent authority evidence.

risk_patterns.name: Delegation lineage mutation
risk_patterns.description: A delegating or forwarding actor rewrites prior lineage hops, making later audit unable to distinguish the forwarded representation from the chain originally received.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Prior-hop mutation destroys independent attribution evidence unless the received representation is retained or integrity-bound.

risk_patterns.name: Delegation evidence-state collapse
risk_patterns.description: Missing, unresolvable, invalid, expired or revoked delegation evidence is collapsed into a generic denial or success state, obscuring what was actually established.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Distinct evidence and lifecycle states are necessary for safe enforcement, audit reconstruction and redress.

risk_patterns.name: Delegation evidence cross-context replay
risk_patterns.description: A content or proof reference valid in one trust domain is replayed in another because the referenced commitment is not bound to the relevant context or domain.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Context-free evidence references can preserve byte integrity while misbinding authority semantics.

risk_patterns.name: Delegation lineage correlation exposure
risk_patterns.description: Multi-hop actor lineage unnecessarily discloses durable principal or agent identifiers across contexts, creating a correlation surface beyond what the relying decision requires.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Auditability should not require unnecessary durable cross-context correlation when a less disclosing proof can satisfy the assurance objective.

risk_patterns.name: Commitment authority mismatch
risk_patterns.description: An authenticated or generally authorized actor attempts a material commitment that is not covered by the exact active mandate, scope, constraints or policy at the commitment boundary.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Commitment admission must positively establish current action-specific authority rather than infer it from identity or general authorization.
guardrail_requirement.condition: exact action authority is not positively established

risk_patterns.name: Approval not bound to exact commitment
risk_patterns.description: A human or organizational approval is accepted for a materially different, superseded or stale action than the commitment being admitted.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Approval must be bound to the exact commitment digest and current policy context.
guardrail_requirement.condition: approval binding is absent, mismatched or stale

risk_patterns.name: Reputation or capability substituted for authority
risk_patterns.description: Reputation, capability advertisement, assurance posture or technical ability is treated as permission to create a material commitment.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Advisory or technical signals must not enlarge principal-derived authority.
guardrail_requirement.condition: non-authority evidence is used as an authorization grant

risk_patterns.name: Commitment authority cannot be reconstructed
risk_patterns.description: A later verifier cannot establish which mandate, policy, status, approval and exact action were evaluated when a material commitment was admitted or rejected.

guardrail_requirement.rationale: Material authority decisions need replayable evidence sufficient to distinguish historical authority from present state.
guardrail_requirement.condition: decision provenance or time-specific authority evidence is unavailable

guardrail_patterns.name: No unilateral irreversible governance action
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: One actor can make an irreversible high-impact governance decision without defined independent check or later remedy.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: No role substitution
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A verifier substitutes one identity/role layer for another without an explicit binding rule.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: No unnecessary disclosure
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A required flow discloses information not necessary for the stated decision or function.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: No essential-service single path
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A high-impact or essential participation path has no viable alternative for foreseeable legitimate users excluded by the primary mechanism.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: No agent action beyond current mandate
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: An autonomous agent performs a consequential action outside the current bounded mandate.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: No unsafe replay
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A replay or retry can repeat an externally consequential side effect without a new authorized decision.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: No consequential decision without contestability evidence
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A high-impact adverse decision is made without sufficient retained evidence and an accountable appeal/remedy path.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: No implicit cross-spec semantic substitution
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A fact established by one specification is treated as establishing a different authority, completion, identity or status fact in another without an explicit contract.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: Critical dependency must have governed exit
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A critical dependency can materially change access or surveillance conditions with no documented alternative, exit or governance response.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before entering or continuing the prohibited state

guardrail_patterns.name: Consequential delegated action needs provenance
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A consequential delegated or agentic action happens without durable evidence linking the action to the accountable principal and the authority used.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before a consequential delegated action is accepted as authorized or complete
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: block, suspend, or mark the action as not sufficiently attributable

guardrail_patterns.name: No unsafe governance transition
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A governance or policy change takes effect for live artefacts or dependent systems without clear effective dates, migration rules, compatibility handling or retirement rules.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before a changed rule becomes effective for existing participants or artefacts
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: delay activation or require an explicit governed transition plan

guardrail_patterns.name: Registry authority must be explicit
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: Trust-relevant registry entries can be added, changed, suspended, removed or corrected without a published rule saying who has authority and how decisions can be reviewed.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before a registry decision changes trust-relevant state
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: do not treat the registry decision as authoritative until the governance rule is established

guardrail_patterns.name: No credential use outside its bound context
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A credential is relied on outside its bound task, audience, purpose or authorization context without an explicit rule permitting the broader use.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before a credential is accepted for a materially different context, audience or purpose
guardrail_patterns.enforcement_point: credential verification and relying-party decision boundary
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: reject, request fresh evidence, or require explicit onward authorization

guardrail_patterns.name: No silent assurance downgrade on dependency failure
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A system treats stale, cached or unavailable trust-relevant dependency state as current without a declared and bounded fallback rule.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: when current dependency or discovery state cannot be obtained or verified
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: deny, defer, or use only a documented bounded fallback with visible risk state

guardrail_patterns.name: Systemic invalidation needs a continuity path
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: Withdrawal, compromise or deregistration of a shared dependency invalidates many downstream artefacts without notification, re-verification, replacement or recovery handling.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before or when a shared dependency is withdrawn, compromised or materially changes status
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: enter a governed continuity or recovery state rather than silently invalidating downstream use

guardrail_patterns.name: Cross-spec lifecycle semantics must reconcile
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A consequential composed action proceeds when participating specifications disagree about the relevant validity, freshness, expiry, revocation or status point.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before a composed action relies on state from more than one specification
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: block or require an explicit lifecycle reconciliation contract

guardrail_patterns.name: No unnecessary cross-context correlation
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: Stable identifiers or combined protocol data enable cross-context correlation that is not needed for the declared purpose.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before stable identifiers or combined data are disclosed across contexts
guardrail_patterns.enforcement_point: identifier creation and presentation composition boundary
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: use scoped identifiers, reduce disclosure, or document why correlation is necessary

guardrail_patterns.name: No load-bearing uniqueness claim without evidence
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A consequential decision relies on a uniqueness or one-person-one-actor claim when the system cannot state and support the scope and mechanism of that claim.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before uniqueness is used to allow, deny, rank, limit or allocate something consequential
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: do not use uniqueness as a decision input, or narrow the claim to what can be supported

guardrail_patterns.name: High-impact recovery must resist takeover
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A recovery path for a high-impact account or identity can bypass normal protections without independent checks, notice, delay or equivalent takeover resistance.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before recovery changes control of a high-impact identity, account or credential
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: stop recovery or require stronger independent recovery evidence

guardrail_patterns.name: No authority from lineage alone
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A consequential delegated action is authorized solely because a caller-supplied actor or delegation chain is internally well formed.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before delegated authority is relied upon
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: block, defer, or escalate until independent authority evidence is established

guardrail_patterns.name: No silent lineage rewrite
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: A forwarding actor modifies a prior delegation hop while the system continues to represent the lineage as append-only audit history.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: on delegated forwarding
guardrail_patterns.failure_mode: reject or record a mutation finding

guardrail_patterns.name: No cross-context authority by replay
guardrail_patterns.prohibited_state: Delegation evidence from one context is accepted as authority in another without a valid context/domain binding.
guardrail_patterns.trigger_condition: before cross-context evidence reliance

assurance_patterns.name: Authentication/authorization separation test
assurance_patterns.assertion: Identity or credential validity alone never authorizes a consequential action.
preconditions: system or specification exposes the relevant decision boundary
assurance_patterns.procedure: Exercise positive and negative cases at the stated boundary and inspect recorded evidence.
assurance_patterns.expected_result: Identity or credential validity alone never authorizes a consequential action.
assurance_patterns.failure_interpretation: The claimed control or guardrail is not demonstrated for the tested condition.

assurance_patterns.name: Critical dependency exit test
assurance_patterns.assertion: A critical dependency has explicit control ownership, material-change monitoring, a governed response and a viable exit or substitution path.
preconditions: deployment relies on a critical external or concentrated dependency
assurance_patterns.procedure: Simulate a material access, price, surveillance, policy or availability change and verify the documented governance and exit response.
assurance_patterns.expected_result: The deployment identifies the responsible authority and can preserve or deliberately suspend service without silently accepting changed dependency conditions.
assurance_patterns.failure_interpretation: Critical dependency power is not effectively governed or the claimed exit path is not credible.

assurance_patterns.name: Actor-lineage authority separation test
assurance_patterns.assertion: Actor or delegation lineage remains attribution evidence only; independent grant evidence, append-only integrity and context binding are tested before consequential authority is inferred.
preconditions: system or specification carries multi-hop actor or delegation lineage
assurance_patterns.procedure: Exercise fabricated-but-monotone, scope-escalation, prior-hop-mutation, missing/unresolvable/invalid evidence, revocation/expiry and cross-context replay cases; inspect retained received/forwarded lineage evidence and the independently resolved authority decision.
assurance_patterns.expected_result: Lineage well-formedness never establishes authority by itself; prior-hop mutation and context replay are detected or fail closed, and evidence/lifecycle states remain distinguishable.
assurance_patterns.failure_interpretation: The system can convert self-reported lineage into authority, lose audit integrity, or misclassify evidence and lifecycle failures.
